recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core follow-up is needed for FHIR-39246 unless the work group wants broader Patient-page prose beyond the approved extension-definition change; no Extension Pack follow-up is needed for the approved wording based on current checked source.
issue_request: FHIR-39246 was a Published Patient Administration R5 change request, resolved Persuasive with Modification, asking the specification to acknowledge that gender identity may be communicated by a proxy and to describe using Provenance.target with the targetElement extension for the individual-genderIdentity extension.
initial_application: No core commit explicitly tagged FHIR-39246 was found. The requested wording is present in the FHIR Extension Pack source for StructureDefinition/individual-genderIdentity and was added by extension-pack commit 70146942d8ceb95e6f26674e03a92e54449e8fda, which was labeled with the neighboring Gender Harmony issue FHIR-39202.
additional_context: The current core checkout no longer contains the individual-genderIdentity StructureDefinition; core only links to the external extension from the Patient gender/sex narrative and documents element-level Provenance.target generally on the Provenance page. Gender Harmony meeting notes mention FHIR-39246, CDA Provenance, and that extensions had moved out of the base spec, while the Jira record includes the later PA 7-0-3 vote.
reconciliation: No source file in the FHIR core checkout was changed. The requested extension-definition guidance belongs to the FHIR Extension Pack, where the current source already says third-party communication of gender identity can be represented with a Provenance resource whose target refers to the Patient and whose targetElement extension identifies the gender identity extension.
